name: Ferencvárosi TC
content:
Ferencvárosi Torna Club, commonly known as Ferencváros or FTC, is a professional football club based in Budapest, Hungary. Founded in 1899, it is one of the most historic and popular sports organizations in the country. The club competes in the top division of Hungarian football and plays its home matches at the Ferencváros Stadion. Its colors are green and white, and the team is widely recognized by its nickname, “The Green Eagles.”

Ferencváros is the most successful club in Hungarian football history, holding records for the highest number of league titles and domestic cup victories. The team has dominated national competitions over many decades and remains a regular contender for championships. Beyond domestic success, the club achieved its greatest international triumph by winning the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup in 1965 and has also reached several European finals, highlighting its historical presence on the continental stage.

The organization is not limited to football, as it operates as a large multi-sport club with sections in disciplines such as handball, water polo, ice hockey, and athletics. Despite this broad structure, the men’s football team remains the most prominent and widely supported. Today, Ferencváros continues to play a central role in Hungarian sports, combining tradition, strong fan support, and ongoing success both domestically and in European competitions.

name: MTK Budapest FC
content:
MTK Budapest FC is a historic football club based in Budapest, Hungary, founded in 1888. It is one of the oldest and most successful clubs in Hungarian football, traditionally playing in blue and white colors. The team competes in the top division, Nemzeti Bajnokság I, and plays its home matches at the Hidegkuti Nándor Stadion. Over its history, MTK has won numerous domestic trophies, including more than 20 league titles and multiple Hungarian Cups.

The club played a major role in the early development of Hungarian football, winning its first league title in 1904 shortly after joining the top division. During the early 20th century, MTK dominated the national championship, including a period where it won ten league titles in a row. Before World War II, it was considered the most successful team in the country, and its influence extended beyond the pitch, with strong ties to the urban middle class and Jewish community in Budapest.

Internationally, MTK has also had notable achievements, including reaching the final of the European Cup Winners’ Cup in 1964. Although its dominance declined in later decades, the club has remained an important part of Hungarian football, known for developing young talent through its academy system. Today, MTK continues to compete at a high level domestically, maintaining its legacy as one of Hungary’s traditional football powers.

name: Újpest FC
content:
Újpest FC is a Hungarian professional football club based in the Újpest district of Budapest. It was founded in 1885 and is one of the oldest football clubs in Hungary. The team plays in the top division of Hungarian football and is traditionally known for its purple and white colors. Its home ground is the Szusza Ferenc Stadion, located in Budapest.

Throughout its history, Újpest has been one of the most successful clubs in Hungary. The club has won the national league title around twenty times and has also secured multiple Hungarian Cup victories. It has been a consistent top-flight team for over a century, with only a very brief interruption in its early history.

On the international stage, Újpest has achieved notable success, especially in earlier decades. The club won competitions such as the Mitropa Cup and reached the semi-finals of major European tournaments in the 1960s and 1970s. While its dominance has declined in modern times, it remains an important and traditional force in Hungarian football with a strong historical legacy.

name: Budapest Honvéd FC
content:
Budapest Honvéd FC is a professional football club based in Budapest, Hungary, founded in 1909 originally as Kispesti AC. The club became one of the most important teams in Hungarian football, especially after being linked to the Hungarian Army in the mid-20th century. It plays its home matches at the Bozsik Aréna and is traditionally known for its red and black colors.

Honvéd experienced its greatest success during the 1950s, when it became the core of the legendary Hungarian national team often referred to as the “Golden Team.” With players such as Ferenc Puskás, Sándor Kocsis, and József Bozsik, the club dominated domestic football and helped revolutionize the European game. It won multiple league titles during this era and established itself as a powerhouse in Hungary and beyond.

After the golden era, the club went through periods of decline and revival, including strong success again in the 1980s and early 1990s when it won several national championships. In total, Honvéd has secured numerous Hungarian league titles and domestic cups, making it one of the country’s most decorated clubs. Today, it continues to compete in the Hungarian football system, maintaining its historic identity and role in developing Hungarian talent.

name: Debreceni VSC
content:
Debreceni VSC is a professional football club based in Debrecen, Hungary, founded in 1902. The club is one of the most important teams in Hungarian football and is commonly known by the nickname “Loki.” It plays its home matches at the Nagyerdei Stadion and traditionally competes in Hungary’s top division.

The club rose to major domestic prominence in the early 2000s, becoming one of the strongest teams in the country during that period. Debreceni VSC has won multiple national league titles, especially dominating Hungarian football across several seasons in the 2000s and early 2010s. It also became known for its rapid rise from lower divisions to consistent championship contention.

On the international stage, Debrecen has represented Hungary in major European competitions, including appearances in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League group stages. The club is widely recognized for its modern era success and its role in strengthening Hungarian club football in European tournaments.

name: Vasas SC
content:
Vasas SC is a Hungarian sports club based in Budapest, founded in 1911 by iron and metal workers. It is primarily known for its football section, which has traditionally represented the working-class district of Angyalföld. The club’s colours are red and blue, and it plays its home matches at the Illovszky Rudolf Stadion. Vasas is one of the historic teams in Hungarian football with a long-standing presence in the top divisions.

The club experienced its golden era in the late 1950s and 1960s, when it became one of the strongest teams in Hungary. During this period, Vasas won multiple national league titles and achieved significant success in European competitions, including reaching the semi-finals of the European Cup in the 1957–58 season. It also became the most successful Hungarian club in the Mitropa Cup, winning that competition several times.

In later decades, Vasas remained a competitive but less dominant force in Hungarian football, with occasional successes in domestic cup competitions and league campaigns. The club has experienced fluctuations between divisions but continues to be an important part of Hungarian football history. Today, Vasas SC is recognized for its tradition, player development, and its contribution to the legacy of Hungarian sport.

name: Győri ETO FC
content:
Győri ETO FC is a Hungarian professional football club based in Győr, founded in 1904. It is one of the traditional teams in Hungarian football and is known for its green and white colours. The club plays its home matches at ETO Park and has a long history of competing in Hungary’s top divisions.

The club’s golden era came in the 1960s and early 1980s, when it became one of the strongest teams in the country. Győr won the Hungarian league title four times in total and achieved its greatest international success by reaching the semi-finals of the European Cup in the 1964–65 season. During that period, the team also competed against major European clubs and established itself as a respected side in continental football.

In later decades, Győri ETO experienced financial difficulties and fluctuating sporting results, including relegations to lower divisions. However, the club has managed to rebuild and return to higher levels of competition in Hungarian football. Today, it remains an important historic club with a strong tradition and a notable place in the country’s football history.

name: Csepel SC
content:
Csepel SC is a Hungarian sports club based in the Csepel district of Budapest, founded in 1912. The club originally started as a gymnastics association and later developed into a multi-sport organization, with football becoming its most prominent section. It has traditionally represented the working-class island community in southern Budapest and has used several names throughout its history before settling on Csepel SC.

The football team experienced its golden era in the mid-20th century. Csepel SC won the Hungarian top division four times, with championship titles in 1941–42, 1942–43, 1947–48, and 1958–59. During this period, the club was one of the strongest teams in the country and regularly competed at the top level of Hungarian football.

On the international stage, Csepel had limited but notable participation, including appearances in European competitions in the 1960 season. Over time, the club’s football department declined, eventually being dissolved in the early 2000s after financial and structural difficulties. Despite this, Csepel SC remains an important historical name in Hungarian sport, with a long legacy and success across multiple disciplines beyond football.

name: Videoton FC Fehérvár
content:
Videoton FC Fehérvár, also known simply as Fehérvár FC, is a professional football club based in Székesfehérvár, Hungary. The club was originally founded in 1941 under a different name and later became widely known as Videoton, a name derived from a Hungarian industrial company. It has undergone several name changes over the years but remains one of the most recognizable teams in Hungarian football. The club plays its home matches at the Sóstói Stadion and is traditionally associated with red and blue colours.

Domestically, Fehérvár has achieved significant success, winning the Hungarian top division three times, in 2011, 2015, and 2018. The club has also won the Hungarian Cup and several other national trophies, including the League Cup and Super Cup. Its rise to prominence in the 21st century marked it as one of the leading teams in Hungary, regularly competing for titles and maintaining a strong presence in the top tier.

Internationally, the club is best known for reaching the UEFA Cup final in 1985, which remains one of the greatest achievements by a Hungarian club in European competitions. In recent decades, Fehérvár has also participated in UEFA Europa League group stages, reinforcing its reputation on the continental stage. Overall, the club holds an important place in Hungarian football history, combining modern success with notable international performances.

name: Budapesti TC
content:
Budapesti Torna Club (BTC) was a pioneering sports club based in Budapest, Hungary, founded in 1885, with its football section established in 1897. It is widely recognized as the first official football club in Hungary and played a key role in introducing and developing the sport in the country. The club also participated in the first recorded football match in Hungary, organized between its own internal teams.

BTC was one of the founding members of the Hungarian national league and achieved immediate success by winning the first two editions of the Nemzeti Bajnokság I in 1901 and 1902. These early triumphs made the club a dominant force in the initial years of organized football in Hungary. It also took part in early international matches, including games against teams from Austria, marking the beginning of Hungarian clubs’ participation in international football.

After its early success, the club gradually declined in prominence, especially after the introduction of professional football in Hungary. From the mid-1920s onward, it mainly competed at the amateur level and eventually ceased operations during the 1945–46 season. Despite its later decline, Budapesti TC remains historically significant as a founding institution of Hungarian football and an early champion of the national league.

name: Vác FC
content:
Vác FC is a Hungarian football club based in the town of Vác, north of Budapest, founded in 1899. Originally established as a multi-sport association, the club later focused on football and has played its home matches at the local municipal stadium. Over its long history, the team has undergone numerous name changes, often influenced by political and sponsorship factors.

The club’s most successful period came in the late 20th century. Vác reached the top tier of Hungarian football in the late 1980s and became a strong competitor in the early 1990s. Its greatest achievement was winning the Hungarian league title in the 1993–94 season, which remains the club’s only top-division championship. During that era, it also finished as runner-up in the league and reached multiple Hungarian Cup finals.

After its peak years, the club experienced a decline, including relegations and financial difficulties that led to drops into lower divisions. Despite occasional promotions and efforts to rebuild, Vác has not returned to its former top-level success. Today, it continues to compete in the Hungarian football system and is remembered for its notable achievements in the 1990s and its long-standing role in Hungarian football history.

name: CA Oradea
content:
Club Atletic Oradea, commonly known as CA Oradea, is a football club based in Oradea, Romania, originally founded in 1910 when the city was part of Austria-Hungary. The team became one of the early important clubs in the region and competed in both Hungarian and Romanian football systems during its history. It is notable for its green and white colors and its long-standing connection to the local community.

The club achieved a rare distinction in European football by winning national league titles in two different countries. It won the Hungarian championship in 1944 and later the Romanian championship in 1949, as well as the Romanian Cup in 1956. These successes made CA Oradea one of the few clubs to claim top-division titles across national borders, highlighting its historical importance in Central European football.

After World War II, political changes under the communist regime led to frequent name and identity changes, which weakened the club’s stability. Eventually, CA Oradea was dissolved in 1963, ending its original era. Decades later, the club was re-established in 2017 and began rebuilding from the lower divisions, aiming to restore its historical legacy within Romanian football.

name: Dunaújváros FC
content:
Dunaújváros FC was a Hungarian football club based in Dunaújváros, founded in 1952 and dissolved in 2009. Over its history, the club underwent numerous name changes, often reflecting political and industrial influences in the region. It played its home matches at the Dunaferr Arena and spent many seasons moving between the top two tiers of Hungarian football.

In its early years, the team quickly reached the top division but struggled to maintain a stable position, experiencing frequent promotions and relegations. For decades, it remained a mid-level club, with its best pre-modern result being a seventh-place finish in the top league in 1978. Its fortunes changed significantly in the late 1990s when, under the name Dunaferr SE, the club returned to the top division and began its most successful period.

The peak of the club’s history came in the 1999–2000 season, when it won its only Hungarian league title and subsequently competed in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League qualifiers. However, after relegation in 2003 and the loss of major financial backing, the club declined rapidly. Despite brief attempts to rebuild, it ultimately withdrew from competition and ceased operations in 2009, ending its existence as a professional team.

name: Zalaegerszegi TE
content:
Zalaegerszegi Torna Egylet Football Club, commonly known as Zalaegerszegi TE or ZTE, is a Hungarian professional football club based in the city of Zalaegerszeg. Founded in 1920, the club competes in the top tier of Hungarian football and plays its home matches at the ZTE Arena, which has a capacity of over 11,000 spectators. The team is traditionally associated with blue and white colors and is often referred to by its nickname “Zete.”

Despite its long history, the club achieved its greatest domestic success relatively late. Zalaegerszeg won its first and only Hungarian league title in the 2001–02 season, marking a major milestone in its development. It has also enjoyed success in cup competitions, winning the Hungarian Cup in 2023 and finishing as runner-up in earlier editions. These achievements established the club as a competitive side in modern Hungarian football.

On the international stage, ZTE has participated in European competitions, most notably in the 2002–03 UEFA Champions League qualifiers, where it famously defeated Manchester United in the first leg before being eliminated overall. Although it has not been a regular presence in European tournaments, the club remains an important part of Hungary’s football landscape, combining regional identity with notable moments of success.

name: Magyar AC
content:
Magyar Atlétikai Club (Magyar AC or MAC) is one of the oldest sports clubs in Hungary, founded in 1875 in Budapest. Originally established as a multi-sport organization, it played an important role in introducing and developing modern athletics and outdoor sports in the country. Over time, the club became part of Hungary’s early sporting culture, particularly among the urban middle class.

The football section of Magyar AC was formed in the late 19th century and was among the early participants in organized Hungarian football. The team joined the top division in 1903 and remained there for many seasons, achieving its best results with runner-up finishes in the league and cup competitions during the early 1900s. These achievements made it a notable club in the formative years of Hungarian football.

Despite its early importance, the club gradually declined, and its football department was dissolved in 1928. The organization itself ceased operations in 1945 but was later re-established in 1988, continuing mainly as a sports association rather than a major football force. Today, Magyar AC is remembered for its pioneering role in Hungarian sport and its contribution to the early development of football in the country.

name: Tatabányai SC
content:
Tatabányai SC is a Hungarian football club based in Tatabánya, founded in 1910. It is one of the traditional provincial teams in Hungarian football and plays its home matches at the Stadion Gyula Grosics. Over its long history, the club has competed across different levels of the national league system, including the top division and the second tier.

The club developed in an industrial mining region and became the most popular team in its city during the early 20th century. Although it struggled financially during the introduction of professionalism, it managed to reach the top division after World War II and later established itself as a competitive side. Tatabánya enjoyed several strong periods, including runner-up finishes in the Hungarian league and appearances in domestic cup finals.

Internationally, the club has participated in European competitions such as the UEFA Cup and Intertoto Cup, achieving some notable results despite not winning major continental trophies. In modern times, Tatabányai SC has experienced fluctuations between divisions, including relegations and rebuilds, but continues to represent an important part of Hungarian football history and regional sporting identity.

name: Paksi FC
content:
Paksi FC is a Hungarian professional football club based in the town of Paks, founded in 1952. The team plays in the top division of Hungarian football and hosts its matches at the Fehérvári úti Stadion. Its traditional colours are green and white, and the club is commonly known by the nickname “Atomcsapat,” reflecting the presence of Hungary’s only nuclear power plant in the city.

For much of its history, the club competed in lower regional and national leagues before achieving promotion to the top tier for the first time in 2006. Paksi quickly established itself as a competitive side, with one of its early highlights being a runner-up finish in the 2010–11 season, which qualified the team for European competition.

In recent years, Paksi FC has continued to strengthen its position in Hungarian football, achieving high league placements and notable domestic success. The club has won the Hungarian Cup multiple times and regularly competes near the top of the league standings. Overall, it represents a modern and steadily growing force in Hungarian football while maintaining a strong local identity.

name: Puskás Akadémia FC
content:
Puskás Akadémia FC is a Hungarian professional football club based in Felcsút, founded in 2005 as part of a football academy named after legendary Hungarian player Ferenc Puskás. The club was created with a strong focus on youth development and operates the Pancho Aréna as its home stadium. Although it began as an academy project, it quickly became an independent senior team competing in Hungary’s league system.

The club rose through the divisions in the 2010s, earning promotion to the top tier and establishing itself as a regular participant in the Nemzeti Bajnokság I. Over time, Puskás Akadémia developed into a competitive side capable of challenging for high league positions, often finishing near the top half of the table. It has also become known for integrating academy graduates into professional football while also recruiting experienced players to strengthen its squad.

In recent years, Puskás Akadémia has regularly qualified for European competitions such as the UEFA Conference League, reflecting its growing sporting ambitions. The club has also finished high in the domestic league, including second-place finishes that secured continental qualification. Today, it is seen as one of the more ambitious modern clubs in Hungary, combining academy-focused development with top-flight competitiveness.

name: Magyar Úszó Egylet
content:
Magyar Úszó Egylet (MÚE) was a Hungarian sports club based in Budapest, founded in 1893. It originally started as a swimming-focused association but soon became a multi-sport club, including an early and important football section. The club was among the pioneers of football in Hungary and played a key role in the formation of organized competitions in the country.

The football team of MÚE joined the first Hungarian national league season in 1901, making it one of the founding participants of top-level competition in Hungary. In that inaugural season, the club achieved strong results and finished as runner-up, marking its best early achievement. During the following years, it remained part of the early development of Hungarian league football but gradually lost competitiveness compared to stronger clubs.

Over time, the club declined in sporting performance and eventually withdrew from top-level football. Its football section ceased operations in the mid-20th century, and the entire club was dissolved in 1948 after several reorganizations and name changes. Despite its disappearance, Magyar Úszó Egylet is remembered as one of the founding institutions of Hungarian football and an important contributor to the sport’s early structure.

name: Budapesti Postás SE
content:
Budapesti Postás SE is a Hungarian sports club based in Budapest, founded in 1899 as an organization originally connected to postal and telegraph workers. It developed as a multi-sport association, and its football section quickly became one of its most notable branches. The club is traditionally associated with green and white colours and played its home matches in Budapest, mainly at the Róna Street sports ground.

The football team was among the early participants in Hungarian organised football, joining the national league in the early 1900s. It achieved strong early results, including finishing near the top of the championship in its first seasons and even winning lower-division titles before and after World War I. Over time, the club experienced several interruptions, reorganisations, and name changes, which affected its stability and long-term competitiveness.

In later decades, Postás SE continued to exist mainly in lower divisions and regional competitions, with its most successful era remaining in the early 20th century. The football department went through multiple mergers and revivals, but it never returned to top-tier prominence. Despite this, the club remains historically important as one of the early contributors to Hungarian football development and league history.

name: Törekvés SE
content:
Törekvés SE is a Hungarian football club based in Budapest, founded in 1900. It originated as a workers’ sports association in the Kőbánya district and developed into one of the early football clubs in the capital. The team was among the pioneers of organized football in Hungary and participated in the early years of the national championship, contributing to the formation of competitive league football in the country.

During the first decades of its existence, the club spent a significant amount of time in Hungary’s top division, with its strongest era coming in the 1910s. Its best league result was a runner-up finish in the 1916–17 season, along with several other high placements in the pre-professional era. After the introduction of professionalism, Törekvés gradually lost ground compared to stronger and better-funded clubs, but it remained an active participant in Hungarian football for many years.

In the later 20th century, the club moved between lower divisions and underwent several name changes and reorganisations, reflecting broader changes in Hungarian sport and society. It never returned to top-level prominence and eventually faded from the highest tiers of competition. Despite this, Törekvés SE is remembered as an important historical club that played a role in the early development of football in Budapest and Hungary.

name: Pécsi MFC
content:
Pécsi MFC is a Hungarian professional football club based in Pécs, founded in 1950 and later reorganised in 1973 through the merger of several local clubs. It is one of the most traditional teams in southern Hungary and plays its home matches at the Stadion PMFC. The club is known for its red and black identity and has spent much of its history moving between the top two divisions of Hungarian football.

Throughout its history, Pécs has experienced several notable periods of success. The club has competed in the top division for many seasons, with strong eras in the 1980s and early 1990s, including a Hungarian Cup victory in 1990. It has also achieved high league finishes and participated in European competitions such as the Cup Winners’ Cup and UEFA Cup, facing well-known international opponents.

In more recent years, the club has faced financial difficulties and instability, which led to relegations and restructuring within the Hungarian league system. Despite these challenges, Pécsi MFC has remained active and continues to compete, maintaining its role as an important regional club with a long football tradition in Hungarian sport.

name: Budapesti VSC
content:
Budapesti VSC (BVSC) is a Hungarian sports club based in Budapest, founded in 1911 as a railway workers’ association. It later developed into a multi-sport club, with its football section becoming one of its key departments. The club is traditionally associated with the Zugló district and has spent most of its history competing in the lower and middle tiers of Hungarian football, with its home matches played at the Szőnyi úti Stadion.

BVSC’s football team has experienced a fluctuating history, including periods of inactivity and rebuilding. After a long absence from senior competition, the club restarted its adult football section in 2012 and gradually climbed through the regional leagues. In the early 2020s, BVSC achieved steady progress, earning promotions from Budapest regional divisions into the national league system. The club also strengthened its structure with new coaching appointments and a focus on returning to professional-level football.

In recent seasons, BVSC has continued its upward development, reaching the second tier of Hungarian football (Nemzeti Bajnokság II) after strong performances in the third division. The team has established itself again as a competitive professional side, aiming to stabilize its position and potentially return to the top division. Today, Budapesti VSC is seen as a historic Budapest club rebuilding its presence in modern Hungarian football.

name: Kisvárda FC
content:
Kisvárda FC is a Hungarian football club based in the town of Kisvárda, founded in 1911. It originally started as a local sports association supported by village merchants and community members. Over the decades, the club went through several reorganizations and name changes, but it remained an important representative of football in northeastern Hungary. It plays its home matches at the Várkerti Stadion.

For most of its history, Kisvárda competed outside the top division, spending long periods in lower leagues. The modern rise of the club began in the 2010s, when it steadily improved its results and structure. A key breakthrough came in the 2017–18 season, when the team finished second in the second division and earned promotion to the top tier of Hungarian football for the first time.

After reaching the top division, Kisvárda established itself as a stable first-league club, achieving solid mid-table finishes and occasionally competing for European qualification spots. The club has also taken part in domestic cup competitions and made its debut in European tournaments in the 2020s. Today, it is regarded as a modern, fast-developing team that has grown significantly compared to its earlier lower-league status.

name: Kecskeméti TE
content:
Kecskeméti TE is a Hungarian football club based in the city of Kecskemét, founded in 1911 as Kecskeméti Testedző Egyesület. It was originally created as a local sports association with strong community involvement, especially from workers and local residents. The club plays its home matches at the Széktói Stadion and is traditionally associated with purple and white colours.

For most of its history, Kecskemét competed in the lower divisions of Hungarian football, with only occasional appearances in the top tier. The club’s modern breakthrough came in the 2000s and early 2010s, when it rapidly climbed the league system. Its most significant achievement was winning the Hungarian Cup in the 2010–11 season, which also earned it qualification for European competition.

In recent years, Kecskeméti TE has established itself as a competitive top-flight club, even achieving a remarkable second-place finish in the Hungarian league in the 2022–23 season. This success allowed the team to compete in European qualifiers, marking one of the strongest periods in its history. Today, the club is considered a stable and ambitious side within Hungarian football.

name: Szombathelyi Haladás
content:
Szombathelyi Haladás is a Hungarian football club based in Szombathely, founded in 1919. The club’s name “Haladás” means “progress,” and it has traditionally represented the city and its surrounding region. It plays its home matches at the Haladás Sportkomplexum and is known for its green and white colours.

Throughout its history, Haladás has spent many seasons in Hungary’s top division and is considered a long-standing member of the national football system. One of its main achievements is reaching the final of the Hungarian Cup on multiple occasions, including in 1975, 1993, and 2002. The club has also had several strong league periods and a reputation as a competitive mid-to-top level side in different eras.

In European competitions, Haladás has had limited but notable appearances, participating in tournaments such as the UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup and UEFA Europa League qualifiers. While it has not achieved major international success, these matches have contributed to its profile beyond Hungary. Today, the club continues to compete mainly in the lower tiers at times, but remains an important part of Hungarian football tradition.

name: Békéscsaba 1912 Előre
content:
Békéscsaba 1912 Előre is a Hungarian football club based in Békéscsaba, founded in 1912 as Előre Munkás Testedző Egyesület. It was created as a workers’ sports association and gradually developed into the city’s main football team. The club is known by its nickname “Lilák” (The Purples) and plays its home matches at the Kórház utcai Stadion. Over its history, it has become an important representative of football in southeastern Hungary.

The club’s most successful period came in the 1980s, highlighted by winning the Hungarian Cup in the 1987–88 season, which remains its greatest achievement. Throughout its history, Békéscsaba has spent around 25 seasons in Hungary’s top division, often moving between the first and second tiers. It also achieved notable league results in different eras and occasionally competed in European tournaments during its peak years.

In modern times, Békéscsaba has experienced frequent promotions and relegations between divisions. The club returned to the top flight in the mid-2010s but was relegated again after a short stay. Despite these fluctuations, it remains an active and historically significant team in Hungarian football, continuing to represent its region with a strong local identity and long tradition.

name: Diósgyőri VTK
content:
Diósgyőri VTK is a Hungarian football club based in Miskolc, founded in 1910 as a workers’ sports association connected to the local ironworks. It is one of the traditional clubs in Hungarian football and is known for its red and white colours. The team has spent most of its history moving between the top two divisions, but it is especially recognized for its strong local identity and passionate fan base.

The club’s most successful era came in the late 1970s and early 1980s. During this period, Diósgyőr won the Hungarian Cup twice and achieved its best league result with a third-place finish in the 1978–79 season. It also gained international attention through European competitions, where it recorded notable victories against established clubs and reached multiple rounds in UEFA tournaments.

In later decades, the club experienced financial problems, relegations, and even bankruptcy in the early 2000s, followed by a supporter-driven revival. Since then, Diósgyőr has returned to professional football and spent several seasons in the top division, including a long uninterrupted stay in the 2010s. Today, it remains one of Hungary’s most traditional provincial clubs, known for its loyal supporters and strong regional significance.

name: Salgótarjáni BTC
content:
Salgótarjáni Barátok Torna Club (SBTC) is a Hungarian football club based in Salgótarján, founded in 1920. The club developed as a workers’ team in an industrial mining city and became one of the most important sporting organizations in the region. It is known by the nickname “Stécé” and traditionally plays in black and white colours. The team competes in the Hungarian football league system and has a long history of fluctuating between divisions.

During its peak periods, SBTC was a strong presence in Hungarian football. The club achieved its best league result with a third-place finish in the top division in the early 1970s and also won the second division multiple times. It reached several Hungarian Cup finals but never managed to win the competition, although it was a regular contender in earlier decades. The club even participated in European competition in the 1970s, representing Hungary on the continental stage.

In later years, Salgótarján experienced decline due to financial difficulties and structural changes in Hungarian football. It spent most of its modern existence in lower divisions, with occasional promotions back to higher tiers but without long-term stability. Today, the club continues to operate in the lower leagues, maintaining its historical identity as one of the traditional provincial teams of Hungarian football with a strong local heritage and past achievements.

name: Ferar Cluj
content:
Ferar Cluj was a football club from Cluj-Napoca, founded in 1907–1918 depending on the source, originally as Kolozsvári Atlétikai Club. It became one of the early football teams in Transylvania and competed in both the Hungarian and Romanian football systems due to the region’s changing political status. The club represented an important part of early Central European football development.

During the interwar and World War II periods, Ferar Cluj played in Romanian regional leagues and later in the Hungarian championship when Transylvania temporarily returned to Hungarian administration. Its strongest era came in the early 1940s, when the club finished third in the Hungarian top division in 1943–44 and reached the Hungarian Cup final in the same period.

After World War II, the club competed briefly in the Romanian top division but was unable to maintain stability. In 1948, Ferar Cluj merged with CFR Cluj and ceased to exist as an independent club. Despite its dissolution, it is remembered for its rare achievement of competing successfully in both Hungarian and Romanian top-flight football and for its notable results during the wartime period.

name: Szolnoki MÁV FC
content:
Szolnoki MÁV FC is a Hungarian football club based in Szolnok, founded on 11 May 1910 as a team connected to the national railway company. It developed as a traditional workers’ club and is historically linked to the city’s industrial background. The team plays its home matches at the Tiszaligeti Stadion and has spent most of its existence moving between the top and lower divisions of Hungarian football.

The club’s most successful period came in the first half of the 20th century. It reached the Hungarian top division multiple times and achieved its greatest success in 1941, when it won the Hungarian Cup by defeating Salgótarjáni BTC in the final. The following season it also recorded one of its best league performances, finishing third in the national championship, marking the peak of its sporting achievements.

After World War II, Szolnoki MÁV FC gradually lost its top-tier status and spent decades mainly in the second division, with occasional appearances in the highest league. The club has experienced frequent fluctuations between divisions in modern times but continues to compete in the Hungarian football system. Today it is regarded as a traditional provincial team with a long history and strong local identity.

name: Szegedi AK
content:
Szegedi AK (Szegedi Atlétikai Klub) is a historic Hungarian football club based in Szeged, founded in 1899. It began as a multi-sport association and became one of the early football teams in Hungary, playing a key role in the development of organized football in the region. The club went through several name changes throughout its existence, reflecting different eras of Hungarian sport and politics, and spent many years competing in the national league system.

The team made its debut in the Hungarian top division in the 1926–27 season, finishing seventh in its first campaign. Over the following decades, Szegedi AK accumulated more than 20 seasons in the top flight, with its strongest period coming in the interwar and early post-war years. One of its notable achievements was reaching the Hungarian Cup final in 1929–30, while it also recorded respectable league finishes, including a third-place result in the early 1940s.

After World War II, the club gradually lost its top-level stability, moving between divisions and undergoing multiple reorganizations and mergers. Despite brief returns to higher tiers, it was unable to re-establish itself as a permanent top-flight team. In 1976, Szegedi AK was merged into Szegedi EAC, effectively ending its independent existence, though its legacy remains tied to the early history of football in Szeged and Hungarian league football overall.

name: Bocskai FC
content:
Bocskai FC was a Hungarian football club based in Debrecen, founded in 1926. It was created as a city team representing the local community and quickly became part of the national football system. The club played its home matches in Debrecen and was active during the interwar period, a time when Hungarian football was becoming more organized and competitive.

During its existence, Bocskai FC competed in Hungary’s top division for several seasons and achieved some notable results. Its greatest success came in the 1929–30 season when the club won the Hungarian Cup, which remains its only major trophy. The team also finished high in the league in the early 1930s, including a strong third-place performance in one of its best seasons.

The club continued to play in the top flight throughout the 1930s but gradually lost stability. Bocskai FC was dissolved in 1940, ending its existence after about 14 years at professional level. Despite its relatively short lifespan, it is remembered as one of the notable Hungarian teams of the interwar era, especially for its cup victory and early contribution to football in Debrecen.

name: Budapesti AK
content:
Budapesti AK (Budapesti Atlétikai Klub, often shortened to BAK) is a Hungarian football club based in Budapest, founded in 1900. It was created by former members of MTK who established their own sports association at the beginning of the 20th century. The club became one of the early participants in organized Hungarian football and was part of the first generations of teams competing in the national league system.

During its early decades, BAK played in Hungary’s top division and spent a significant period among the strongest teams in the country. Its best achievement came in the early 1910s when it finished third in the national championship, and it also reached the Hungarian Cup final during the pre-war era. The club remained a regular first-division participant until the early 1920s, after which its performance declined and it was unable to re-establish itself among the top clubs.

Following the introduction of professional football and later reorganisations of the Hungarian league system, Budapesti AK gradually fell into lower divisions and eventually disappeared from top-level competition. The original club was dissolved in 1947 after several structural changes and a long period of decline. In 2018, the name was revived by a modern amateur club, continuing the historical identity in lower-tier Budapest football.

name: Nemzeti SC
content:
Nemzeti SC (Nemzeti Sport Club) was a Hungarian football club based in Budapest, founded in 1906. It originated in the Terézváros district and developed as one of the early clubs participating in organized football in Hungary. The team competed in the early national championship system and became part of the first generation of Budapest-based clubs shaping Hungarian football culture.

The club’s strongest period came in the first decades of the 20th century. It made its top-flight debut in 1909–10 and achieved its best league result immediately, finishing third in the national championship. In later years, Nemzeti SC remained a regular participant in the Hungarian league system, though it struggled to consistently compete with the strongest Budapest clubs and moved between divisions over time.

After several reorganizations and interruptions, the club gradually declined. It experienced periods of inactivity during and after World War II, and although it was briefly re-established, it ultimately ceased operations in the mid-20th century. Despite its disappearance, Nemzeti SC is remembered as one of the early contributors to Hungarian football development and the foundation era of the national league.

name: 33 FC
content:
33 FC was a Hungarian football club based in Óbuda, Budapest, founded in 1900. It was one of the early clubs in Hungarian football and took part in the first seasons of the national championship. The team is known by its black and white colours and became one of the pioneering sides during the formative years of organised football in Hungary.

The club achieved its best early success in the 1902 season, when it finished third in the Hungarian top division. In the following years, 33 FC remained a regular participant in the league, spending many seasons in the first division during the early 20th century. Although it was competitive in its early decades, it gradually struggled to keep pace with stronger Budapest clubs and experienced multiple relegations and promotions over time.

After several name changes and reorganisations during the mid-20th century, including periods under industrial and worker-related identities, the club eventually lost stability. It was dissolved in 1958, ending its professional era after nearly six decades of existence. Despite this, 33 FC is remembered as one of the early contributors to Hungarian football development and one of the original clubs of the national league system.

name: FC Sopron
content:
FC Sopron was a Hungarian football club based in the city of Sopron, founded in 1921. It began as a local sports association and over time developed into a professional football team representing the western border region of Hungary. The club played its home matches at the Városi Stadion and was known for its white and red colours.

The team spent much of its history in the lower divisions, but it reached the top tier of Hungarian football in the early 2000s. Its greatest success came in the 2004–05 season, when it won the Hungarian Cup, the most important trophy in its history. This achievement also allowed the club to participate in European competitions, marking the peak of its sporting success.

However, financial problems and administrative instability led to its rapid decline. In 2008, the club lost its league licence due to unpaid debts and taxes, which resulted in its exclusion from the competition and eventual dissolution. After its collapse, a new club was formed in Sopron to continue football in the city, but FC Sopron itself ceased to exist as a professional entity.

name: BFC Siófok
content:
BFC Siófok is a Hungarian football club based in the town of Siófok on the shore of Lake Balaton, founded in 1921. It began as a local sports association and gradually developed into a professional football team representing the region. The club is traditionally known for its yellow and blue colours and plays its home matches at the Révész Géza utcai Stadion.

Throughout its history, Siófok has mainly competed in the lower and middle levels of Hungarian football, but it has had several periods in the top division. Its most successful moment came in 1984, when it won the Hungarian Cup, the biggest trophy in its history. The club has also achieved strong league performances, including a fourth-place finish in the top division in the early 1990s, marking its peak era.

In modern times, BFC Siófok has moved between divisions and experienced several reorganisations and financial changes. It has spent many seasons in the second tier, with occasional promotions and relegations shaping its recent history. Today, it remains an active Hungarian club with a long tradition and a stable presence in the national league system, representing its coastal city and regional football culture.

name: Soroksár SC
content:
Soroksár SC is a Hungarian football club based in the Soroksár district of Budapest, founded in 1905. It developed as a local community team and gradually became part of the national football structure. The club plays its home matches at the Szamosi Mihály Sporttelep and is traditionally known for its yellow and black colours.

For most of its history, Soroksár competed outside the top division, spending many years in lower tiers of Hungarian football. The club experienced various reorganisations and periods of instability during the 20th century, but it maintained its presence in regional and national competitions. In modern times, it has become a more stable professional side, regularly competing in the second division (NB II).

Today, Soroksár SC is established as a consistent NB II club, often finishing in mid-table positions and focusing on player development and competitiveness within the second tier. It is also closely linked with larger Budapest football structures through cooperation agreements, which help strengthen its squad and sporting level. Overall, the club represents a stable second-division team with a long local tradition and modern professional structure.

name: III. Kerületi TVE
content:
III. Kerületi TVE is a Hungarian football club based in the Óbuda district of Budapest, founded in 1887, making it one of the oldest sports associations in the country. Originally established as a gymnastics and fencing club, it later developed a football section that became part of Hungary’s early football history. The club colours are blue and white, and it plays its home matches at the Hévízi úti Stadion.

The team became a regular participant in the Hungarian top division in the early 20th century, spending many seasons at the highest level between the 1910s and 1930s. Its greatest achievement came in the 1930–31 season when it won the Hungarian Cup by defeating Ferencváros in the final. During this era, the club also achieved several strong league finishes and was considered a competitive Budapest side in national football.

After its early peak, III. Kerületi TVE gradually declined from top-level football and moved between lower divisions over the following decades. It underwent multiple reorganisations, mergers, and name changes, especially during the mid-20th century, reflecting broader changes in Hungarian sport. In modern times, the club has re-established itself as an active lower-division team and continues to represent its historic Óbuda roots in Hungarian football.

name: Komlói Bányász SK
content:
Komlói Bányász SK is a Hungarian football club based in Komló, founded in 1922 as a workers’ team linked to the local mining industry. It became the city’s main sports organization and developed a strong identity rooted in the mining community. The club is traditionally associated with blue colours and plays its home matches at the Bányász Stadion.

Throughout its history, Komló mostly competed in the second tier of Hungarian football, but it also reached the top division in several periods, including appearances in the late 1950s and 1960s. One of its notable achievements was finishing high enough in the league to establish itself as a competitive provincial side, and it also reached the Hungarian Cup final in the 1970s. In that era, the club gained national attention and took part in European competition, marking the peak of its sporting success.

In later decades, Komlói Bányász gradually declined from top-level football and spent most of its time in lower divisions. Despite financial and structural difficulties, it remained active and continued to represent its region in Hungarian football. Today, it is regarded as a traditional provincial club with a strong historical connection to the mining community and an important role in the sporting heritage of Komló.

name: Miskolci AK
content:
Miskolci AK (Miskolci Atléta Kör) is a Hungarian football club based in Miskolc, founded in 1926. It developed as a local sports association and became one of the early football teams representing the industrial city. The club participated in the early structure of Hungarian football during the interwar period and contributed to the development of the sport in the region.

The team reached its most notable sporting moment in the late 1920s and early 1930s. Miskolci AK competed in the national league and achieved its best domestic success by finishing high in lower-tier competitions and reaching the Hungarian Cup final in the 1927–28 season. It also took part in the top division for a short period, including its debut in the 1931–32 season.

After its early decades, the club gradually lost its place in higher-level competitions and went through several reorganisations and name changes. By the mid-20th century it was no longer a stable presence in top Hungarian football and eventually disappeared from major competitions. Despite its decline, Miskolci AK remains part of the early football history of Miskolc and is remembered as one of the city’s pioneering clubs.

name: Budapesti EAC
content:
Budapesti EAC (Budapesti Egyetemi Atlétikai Club) is a Hungarian football club based in Budapest, founded in 1898 as part of the Eötvös Loránd University sports association. It is one of the oldest university-based sports clubs in Hungary and originally developed as a multi-sport organization before establishing its football section. The club has traditionally been linked to student and academic communities rather than industrial or working-class roots.

The football team first appeared in the Hungarian league system in the 1920s and competed at national level during its early years. Its most notable sporting achievement was winning the second division title in the 1923–24 season, which allowed it to participate in the top tier. The club also reached the Hungarian Cup final in the mid-1920s, marking the peak period of its football success.

Over time, Budapesti EAC gradually lost its position among the stronger Hungarian clubs and underwent several reorganisations and name changes during the mid-20th century. After periods of decline and structural changes, it eventually moved away from top-level football and became mainly a lower-division or university-oriented sports club. Today, it is remembered as a historic Budapest institution that played a role in the early development of Hungarian football.

name: BKV Előre SC
content:
BKV Előre SC is a Hungarian football club based in Budapest, founded in 1912 as the sports association of the city’s public transport company. It developed as a traditional workers’ club and became part of Hungary’s early football structure. The team plays its home matches at the Sport utca stadium and is known for its yellow and blue colours.

Throughout its history, BKV Előre has mostly competed in the lower and middle tiers of Hungarian football, but it also had several periods in the top division. The club reached the Hungarian Cup final in the 1933–34 season and played multiple seasons in the first league during the 1940s and early 1950s. It also achieved success in the second division, winning it on several occasions, including in the early 2000s.

In modern times, the club has settled mainly in the third tier of Hungarian football, where it continues to compete as a stable lower-league side. Despite not being among the country’s top teams, it remains an established Budapest club with a long tradition and historical role in Hungarian sport.

name: Dorogi FC
content:
Dorogi FC is a Hungarian football club based in the town of Dorog, founded in 1914 as a team closely connected to the local mining industry. It developed as a traditional workers’ club and gradually became the main representative of the city in national football. The team plays its home matches at the Buzánszky Jenő Stadion and is known for its black and red colours.

The club’s strongest period came in the mid-20th century, when it reached the Hungarian top division and achieved notable domestic success. Dorogi FC was a runner-up in the Hungarian Cup in 1952 and also competed regularly in the first division during that era. It had several important players who contributed to Hungarian football and helped the club establish a respected position in national competitions.

In later decades, Dorog moved between divisions and spent much of its history outside the top flight. The club continued to compete in lower tiers, including recent seasons in the third division, where it remains a competitive side with solid performances. Today, Dorogi FC is regarded as a traditional provincial club with a long history and strong ties to its mining-town identity.

name: Mezőkövesdi SE
content:
Mezőkövesdi SE is a Hungarian football club based in the town of Mezőkövesd, founded in 1975. It was established as a local sports association and developed into the city’s main football team over time. The club plays its home matches at the Mezőkövesdi Városi Stadion and is known for its yellow and blue colours, which reflect its modern identity and sponsorship background.

For most of its history, Mezőkövesd competed in the lower divisions of Hungarian football, gradually building its structure and competitiveness. The club’s breakthrough came in the 2010s, when it achieved promotion to the top division for the first time in 2016 after winning promotion from the second tier. Since then, it has established itself as a stable first-league team, often finishing mid-table and occasionally challenging for higher positions.

In recent years, Mezőkövesdi SE has also achieved notable cup and league performances, including reaching the Hungarian Cup final in 2020 and securing strong league finishes in the top division. The club has become known for its steady development, disciplined structure, and ability to compete consistently at the highest national level despite its relatively small size.

name: Budafoki MTE
content:
Budafoki MTE is a Hungarian football club based in the Budafok district of Budapest, founded in 1912. It began as a workers’ sports association and gradually developed into a stable local team. The club plays its home matches at the Promontor utcai Stadion and is traditionally associated with red and black colours. It has long been an important representative of its district within Budapest football.

For most of its history, Budafok competed in the lower divisions of Hungarian football, with many seasons spent outside the top tier. The club’s modern rise began in the 2010s, when it improved its results in the second and third divisions. A major breakthrough came in the 2019–20 season, when it finished second in the second division and earned promotion to the top flight for only the second time in its history.

In recent years, Budafoki MTE has moved between the top two divisions, struggling to fully establish itself as a permanent first-league side. Despite relegation after its return to the top tier, it remains a competitive and well-organised club in the second division. Today, it is seen as a traditional Budapest team with strong local identity and a history of resilience and gradual development.
